_comment: Known vulnerabilities in the Apache HTTP Server itself (not its modules from other projects), used by the Server Side Technology Version with Known Vulnerabilities passive scan rule.
The 'vulnerabilities' array is GENERATED from the CVE records published by the Apache HTTP Server project at https://httpd.apache.org/security/json/ by the Gradle task
':addOns:pscanrules:updateApacheKnownVulnerabilities'; do not hand edit generated entries, they will be overwritten.
Entries with "source": "manual" are preserved by the generator and are for problems the records do not cover.
cve         - the CVE identifier, e.g. CVE-2021-41773.
name        - a short title for the problem, taken from the record.
description - a brief, plain-text description of the problem and its impact.

severity    - one of: critical, high, medium, low. Maps to the ZAP alert risk. The project's 'moderate' and 'important' map to medium and high; records rated 'n/a' (not vulnerabilities in the server itself) are skipped.
affected    - one range per affected release branch (1.3, 2.0, 2.2, 2.4). A version V is affected when introduced <= V < fixed.
Ranges must not overlap each other. Versions are plain dotted numerics as reported in headers (e.g. 2.4.58).
The fixed version is the release of the branch named in the record's timeline, else the version after the highest affected one.
Branches which never received a fix are capped at the start of the next branch, so that they cannot match later branches.
Versions the project lists as only possibly affected form their own range marked "assumed": true, which lowers the alert confidence.
links       - URLs to the project's vulnerabilities page for the branch, the NVD/CVE entry and the CVE record. The first link is treated as the primary reference.
published   - the publication date, or the earliest date in the record's timeline when none is stated.
source      - 'apache-httpd-json' for generated entries, 'manual' for hand maintained ones.

vulnerabilities.name: limited RCE for some internal redirects to non-CGI files in CGI directories
vulnerabilities.description: Deployment of wrong handler vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server allows the target of some internal redirects from CGI programs to also be treated as CGI and executed. The target must already be in a directory enabled for CGI and have no other extension understood by mod_mime.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_dav shared lock overflow
vulnerabilities.description: A memory calculation bug in mod_dav in Apache httpd 2.4.67 and earlier allows an attacker with permission to create WebDAV locks to crash server child processes.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_heartmonitor denial of service
vulnerabilities.description: NULL Pointer Dereference vulnerability in Apache HTTP Servers mod_heartmonitor over unicast listener.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_session: Session cookie not removed during internal redirect
vulnerabilities.description: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server's mod_session_cookie module.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_auth_digest reauthentication attack
vulnerabilities.description: Missing authentication checks in mod_auth_digest in Apache Software Foundation Apache HTTP Server before 2.4.69 on all platforms allows an unauthenticated remote client to cause a denial of service (forced re-authentication) via forged Authorization headers when Digest authentication is enabled with AuthDigestNcCheck .

vulnerabilities.name: mod_charset_lite: Heap overflow in finish_partial_char
vulnerabilities.description: Out-of-bounds Write vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server's mod_charset_lite.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_rewrite use-after-free via %{LA-U:HTTP:...}
vulnerabilities.description: Use After Free vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server's mod_rewrite when using lookahead (%{LA-U:HTTP:...})

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_html: crash in dump_content
vulnerabilities.description: Out-of-bounds Write vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server's mod_proxy_html with crafted HTTP response bodies.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: mod_http2 use-after-free / wild write via shared session->bbtmp re-entrancy
vulnerabilities.description: Use After Free vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http2 via shared session->bbtmp re-entrancy

vulnerabilities.name: mod_dav_fs property database read access
vulnerabilities.description: Internal state files accessible to external parties in mod_dav_fs in Apache Software Foundation Apache HTTP Server before 2.4.69 on all platforms allows a remote client to read WebDAV dead properties of resources it cannot author via a GET request for the .DAV state directory

vulnerabilities.name: Out-of-Bounds Write in ap_directory_walk() Canonical-Name Rewrite on CASE_BLIND_FILESYSTEM
vulnerabilities.description: Out-of-bounds Write vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server on Windows while processing paths with 8.3 names that may grow when expanded.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_ssl SSLRequire allows .htaccess ap_expr file-function
vulnerabilities.description: Improper Privilege Management vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server's mod_ssl via SSLRequire and file-related expressions.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_ftp PASV address handling
vulnerabilities.description: Improper validation of FTP PASV reply address in mod_proxy_ftp in Apache Software Foundation Apache HTTP Server through 2.4.68 on all platforms allows, in forward proxy configurations, an untrusted FTP server to cause the proxy to open a data connection to an arbitrary third-party host via a crafted PASV response.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_vhost_alias stack overflow
vulnerabilities.description: Stack-based buffer overflow in mod_vhost_alias in Apache Software Foundation Apache HTTP Server through 2.4.68 on all platforms allows a remote client to cause a denial of service or potentially execute arbitrary code via an HTTP request with a Host header exceeding 8192 bytes when VirtualDocumentRoot uses a hostname format specifier and LimitRequestFieldSize is raised above the default.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_xml2enc crash on charset conversion failure
vulnerabilities.description: A NULL pointer dereference in mod_xml2enc in Apache Software Foundation Apache HTTP Server before 2.4.69 on all platforms allows an untrusted backend server to cause a denial of service via a proxied response with a charset whose conversion partially succeeds then fails.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_uwsgi Transfer-Encoding response smuggling
vulnerabilities.description: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling') response smuggling vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server via mod_proxy_uwsgi and a crafted uwsgi response with Transfer-Encoding.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_auth_digest one-time-nonce replay attack
vulnerabilities.description: Authentication bypass by capture-replay in mod_auth_digest in Apache Software Foundation Apache HTTP Server 2.4.x on all platforms allows a man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacker to replay captured digest authentication credentials via crafted requests that trigger garbage collection of the client's shared memory entry when AuthDigestNonceLifetime is set to 0.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_auth_digest DoS attack
vulnerabilities.description: Use after free in mod_auth_digest in Apache Software Foundation Apache HTTP Server before 2.4.69 on all platforms allows an unauthenticated remote client to cause authentication state corruption via concurrent Digest authentication requests when AuthDigestNcCheck is enabled or AuthDigestNonceLifetime is set to 0.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_userdir information disclosure
vulnerabilities.description: Path equivalence: '/./' (single dot directory) vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server's mod_userdir module when configured with absolute non-wildcard UserDir directive (the 2nd form in https://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.4/mod/mod_userdir.html#userdir)

vulnerabilities.name: mod_dav_fs namespace overflow
vulnerabilities.description: Integer overflow in mod_dav_fs in Apache HTTP Server through 2.4.68 allows an authenticated WebDAV client with write access to crash worker processes and persistently corrupt a directory's property database via PROPPATCH requests declaring many XML namespaces.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_ldap per-dir use-after-free
vulnerabilities.description: Use After Free vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server with mod_ldap in per-directory configuration

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_ftp XSS
vulnerabilities.description: A cross-site scripting vulnerability exists in mod_proxy_ftp's HTML directory list generation in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.67 and earlier when listing FTP directory contents either via forward or reverse proxy configuration.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_html buffer overflow
vulnerabilities.description: A buffer overflow in mod_proxy_html in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.67 and earlier allows an attack by an untrusted backend. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.4.68, which fixes this issue.

vulnerabilities.name: ProxyPassReverseCookieMap buffer overflow
vulnerabilities.description: Heap-based Buffer Overflow vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server with malicious backend servers and ProxyPassReverseCookie

vulnerabilities.name: mod_dav_fs protected directory access
vulnerabilities.description: A path handling issue in mod_dav_fs in Apache 2.4.67 and earlier allows a WebDAV content author to directly manipulate trusted DAV property databases, potentially causing child process crashes.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_xml2enc heap overflow
vulnerabilities.description: Heap-based Buffer Overflow vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server with mod_xml2enc, xml2StartParse, and untrusted content

vulnerabilities.name: OOB Read in `merge_response_headers` can cause crash
vulnerabilities.description: Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server with mod_headers and mod_mime and multiple response languages.

vulnerabilities.name: escalation of privilege through expressions in .htaccess in multiple modules
vulnerabilities.description: Improper Privilege Management vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.67 and earlier allows local .htaccess authors to read files with the privileges of the httpd user.

vulnerabilities.name: Stack Buffer Over-Read in mod_ssl OCSP `send_request`
vulnerabilities.description: Buffer Over-read vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server via outbound OCSP requests to an attacker controlled OCSP server

vulnerabilities.name: Loop in `proxy_ftp_handler` in mod_proxy_ftp
vulnerabilities.description: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') vulnerability in the mod_proxy_ftp module in Apache HTTP Server with an attacker controlled backend FTP server.

vulnerabilities.name: Heap Underflow in `ap_regname` via Signed Char Overflow
vulnerabilities.description: Buffer Underwrite vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server on crafted regular expressions in the configuration.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_http2 memory corruption when file handles exhausted
vulnerabilities.description: Use After Free vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server module mod_http2 when file handles are already exhausted.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_http2 denial of service
vulnerabilities.description: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http leads to denial of service via malicious HTTP requests.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: http2: double free and possible RCE on early reset
vulnerabilities.description: Double Free and possible RCE vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server with the HTTP/2 protocol.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: mod_rewrite elevation of privileges via ap_expr
vulnerabilities.description: An escalation of privilege bug in various modules in Apache HTTP 2.4.66 and earlier allows local .htaccess authors to read files with the privileges of the httpd user.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: buffer overflow in mod_proxy_ajp via  ajp_msg_check_header()
vulnerabilities.description: Heap-based Buffer Overflow vulnerability in mod_proxy_ajp of Apache HTTP Server. If mod_proxy_ajp connects to a malicious AJP server this AJP server can send a malicious AJP message back to mod_proxy_ajp and cause it to write 4 attacker controlled bytes after the end of a heap based buffer.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: mod_md unrestricted OCSP response
vulnerabilities.description: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server's  mod_md via OCSP response data.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_dav_lock indirect lock crash
vulnerabilities.description: A NULL pointer dereference in mod_dav_lock in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.66 and earlier may allow an attacker to crash the server with a malicious request.mod_dav_lock is not used internally by mod_dav or mod_dav_fs.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_auth_digest timing attack
vulnerabilities.description: A timing attack against mod_auth_digest in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.66 allows a bypass of Digest authentication by a remote attacker.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_authn_socache crash
vulnerabilities.description: A NULL pointer dereference in the mod_authn_socache in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.66 and earlier allows an unauthenticated remote user to crash a child process in a caching forward proxy configuration.

vulnerabilities.name: multiple modules: HTTP response splitting forwarding malicious status line
vulnerabilities.description: HTTP response splitting vulnerability in multiple Apache HTTP Server modules with untrusted or compromised backend servers.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: Off-by-one OOB reads in AJP getter functions
vulnerabilities.description: Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability in mod_proxy_ajp of

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_ajp: Heap Buffer Over-Read Due to Missing Null-Termination Check (ajp_msg_get_string)
vulnerabilities.description: Improper Null Termination, Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: mod_proxy_ajp: Heap Over-Read and memory disclosure in  ajp_parse_data()
vulnerabilities.description: Buffer Over-read vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: mod_md (ACME), unintended retry intervals
vulnerabilities.description: An integer overflow in the case of failed ACME certificate renewal leads, after a number of failures (~30 days in default configurations), to the backoff timer becoming 0. Attempts to renew the certificate then are repeated without delays until it succeeds.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: Server Side Includes adds query string to #exec cmd=...
vulnerabilities.description: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.65 and earlier with Server Side Includes (SSI) enabled and mod_cgid (but not mod_cgi) passes the shell-escaped query string to #exec cmd="..." directives.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: NTLM Leakage on Windows through UNC SSRF
vulnerabilities.description: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: CGI environment variable override
vulnerabilities.description: Improper Neutralization of Escape, Meta, or Control Sequences vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server through environment variables set via the Apache configuration unexpectedly superseding variables calculated by the server for CGI programs.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: mod_userdir+suexec bypass via AllowOverride FileInfo
vulnerabilities.description: mod_userdir+suexec bypass via AllowOverride FileInfo vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server. Users with access to use the RequestHeader directive in htaccess can cause some CGI scripts to run under an unexpected userid.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: 'RewriteCond expr' always evaluates to true in 2.4.64
vulnerabilities.description: A bug in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.64 results in all "RewriteCond expr ..." tests evaluating as "true".

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: HTTP response splitting
vulnerabilities.description: HTTP response splitting in the core of Apache HTTP Server allows an attacker who can manipulate the Content-Type response headers of applications hosted or proxied by the server can split the HTTP response.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: SSRF with mod_headers setting Content-Type header
vulnerabilities.description: SSRF in Apache HTTP Server with mod_proxy loaded allows an attacker to send outbound proxy requests to a URL controlled by the attacker. Requires an unlikely configuration where mod_headers is configured to modify the Content-Type request or response header with a value provided in the HTTP request.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: SSRF on Windows due to UNC paths
vulnerabilities.description: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in Apache HTTP Server on Windows allows to potentially leak NTLM hashes to a malicious server via mod_rewrite or apache expressions that pass unvalidated request input.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: mod_ssl error log variable escaping
vulnerabilities.description: Insufficient escaping of user-supplied data in mod_ssl in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.63 and earlier allows an untrusted SSL/TLS client to insert escape characters into log files in some configurations.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: mod_ssl access control bypass with session resumption
vulnerabilities.description: In some mod_ssl configurations on Apache HTTP Server 2.4.35 through to 2.4.62, an access control bypass by trusted clients is possible using TLS 1.3 session resumption.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: mod_proxy_http2 denial of service
vulnerabilities.description: In certain proxy configurations, a denial of service attack against Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.26 through to 2.4.63 can be triggered by untrusted clients causing an assertion in mod_proxy_http2.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: mod_ssl TLS upgrade attack
vulnerabilities.description: In some mod_ssl configurations on Apache HTTP Server versions through to 2.4.63, an HTTP desynchronisation attack allows a man-in-the-middle attacker to hijack an HTTP session via a TLS upgrade.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: HTTP/2 DoS by Memory Increase
vulnerabilities.description: Late Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: source code disclosure with handlers configured via AddType
vulnerabilities.description: A partial fix for CVE-2024-39884 in the core of Apache HTTP Server 2.4.61 ignores some use of the legacy content-type based configuration of handlers. "AddType" and similar configuration, under some circumstances where files are requested indirectly, result in source code disclosure of local content. For example, PHP scripts may be served instead of interpreted.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: SSRF with mod_rewrite in server/vhost context on Windows
vulnerabilities.description: SSRF in Apache HTTP Server on Windows with mod_rewrite in server/vhost context, allows to potentially leak NTLM hashes to a malicious server via SSRF and malicious requests.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: source code disclosure with handlers configured via AddType
vulnerabilities.description: A regression in the core of Apache HTTP Server 2.4.60 ignores some use of the legacy content-type based configuration of handlers. "AddType" and similar configuration, under some circumstances where files are requested indirectly, result in source code disclosure of local content. For example, PHP scripts may be served instead of interpreted.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: DoS by Null pointer in websocket over HTTP/2
vulnerabilities.description: Serving WebSocket protocol upgrades over a HTTP/2 connection could result in a Null Pointer dereference, leading to a crash of the server process, degrading performance.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server on WIndows UNC SSRF
vulnerabilities.description: SSRF in Apache HTTP Server on Windows allows to potentially leak NTLM hashes to a malicious server via SSRF and malicious requests or content Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.4.60 which fixes this issue. Note: Existing configurations that access UNC paths will have to configure new directive "UNCList" to allow access during request processing.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server proxy encoding problem
vulnerabilities.description: Encoding problem in mod_proxy in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.59 and earlier allows request URLs with incorrect encoding to be sent to backend services, potentially bypassing authentication via crafted requests. This affects configurations where mechanisms other than ProxyPass/ProxyPassMatch or RewriteRule with the 'P' flag are used to configure a request to be proxied, such as SetHandler or inadvertent proxying via CVE-2024-39573. Note that these alternate mechanisms may be used within .htaccess.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server weakness with encoded question marks in backreferences
vulnerabilities.description: Substitution encoding issue in mod_rewrite in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.59 and earlier allows attacker to execute scripts in directories permitted by the configuration but not directly reachable by any URL or source disclosure of scripts meant to only to be executed as CGI.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server weakness in mod_rewrite when first segment of substitution matches filesystem path.
vulnerabilities.description: Improper escaping of output in mod_rewrite in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.59 and earlier allows an attacker to map URLs to filesystem locations that are permitted to be served by the server but are not intentionally/directly reachable by any URL, resulting in code execution or source code disclosure.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server may use exploitable/malicious backend application output to run local handlers via internal redirect
vulnerabilities.description: Vulnerability in core of Apache HTTP Server 2.4.59 and earlier are vulnerably to information disclosure, SSRF or local script execution via backend applications whose response headers are malicious or exploitable.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: Crash resulting in Denial of Service in mod_proxy via a malicious request
vulnerabilities.description: null pointer dereference in mod_proxy in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.59 and earlier allows an attacker to crash the server via a malicious request. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.4.60, which fixes this issue.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: mod_rewrite proxy handler substitution
vulnerabilities.description: Potential SSRF in mod_rewrite in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.59 and earlier allows an attacker to cause unsafe RewriteRules to unexpectedly setup URL's to be handled by mod_proxy. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.4.60, which fixes this issue.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: HTTP response splitting
vulnerabilities.description: Faulty input validation in the core of Apache allows malicious or exploitable backend/content generators to split HTTP responses.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: HTTP Response Splitting in multiple modules
vulnerabilities.description: HTTP Response splitting in multiple modules in Apache HTTP Server allows an attacker that can inject malicious response headers into backend applications to cause an HTTP desynchronization attack.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: HTTP/2 DoS by memory exhaustion on endless continuation frames
vulnerabilities.description: HTTP/2 incoming headers exceeding the limit are temporarily buffered in nghttp2 in order to generate an informative HTTP 413 response. If a client does not stop sending headers, this leads to memory exhaustion.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_macro buffer over-read
vulnerabilities.description: Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability in mod_macro of Apache HTTP Server.This issue affects Apache HTTP Server: through 2.4.57.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: DoS in HTTP/2 with initial windows size 0
vulnerabilities.description: An attacker, opening a HTTP/2 connection with an initial window size of 0, was able to block handling of that connection indefinitely in Apache HTTP Server. This could be used to exhaust worker resources in the server, similar to the well known "slow loris" attack pattern. This has been fixed in version 2.4.58, so that such connection are terminated properly after the configured connection timeout.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: HTTP/2 stream memory not reclaimed right away on RST
vulnerabilities.description: When a HTTP/2 stream was reset (RST frame) by a client, there was a time window were the request's memory resources were not reclaimed immediately. Instead, de-allocation was deferred to connection close. A client could send new requests and resets, keeping the connection busy and open and causing the memory footprint to keep on growing. On connection close, all resources were reclaimed, but the process might run out of memory before that.

vulnerabilities.name: HTTP request splitting with mod_rewrite and mod_proxy
vulnerabilities.description: Some mod_proxy configurations on Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.0 through 2.4.55 allow a HTTP Request Smuggling attack.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: mod_proxy_uwsgi HTTP response splitting
vulnerabilities.description: HTTP Response Smuggling vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server via mod_proxy_uwsgi. This issue affects Apache HTTP Server: from 2.4.30 through 2.4.55.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_dav out of  bounds read, or write of zero byte
vulnerabilities.description: A carefully crafted If: request header can cause a memory read, or write of a single zero byte, in a pool (heap) memory location beyond the header value sent. This could cause the process to crash.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: mod_proxy_ajp Possible request smuggling
vulnerabilities.description: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request Smuggling') vulnerability in mod_proxy_ajp of Apache HTTP Server allows an attacker to smuggle requests to the AJP server it forwards requests to. This issue affects Apache HTTP Server Apache HTTP Server 2.4 version 2.4.54 and prior versions.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server: mod_proxy prior to 2.4.55 allows a backend to trigger HTTP response splitting
vulnerabilities.description: Prior to Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55, a malicious backend can cause the response headers to be truncated early, resulting in some headers being incorporated into the response body. If the later headers have any security purpose, they will not be interpreted by the client.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_ajp: Possible request smuggling
vulnerabilities.description: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request Smuggling') vulnerability in mod_proxy_ajp of Apache HTTP Server allows an attacker to smuggle requests to the AJP server it forwards requests to. This issue affects Apache HTTP Server Apache HTTP Server 2.4 version 2.4.53 and prior versions.

vulnerabilities.name: read beyond bounds in mod_isapi
vulnerabilities.description: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.53 and earlier on Windows may read beyond bounds when configured to process requests with the mod_isapi module.

vulnerabilities.name: read beyond bounds via ap_rwrite()
vulnerabilities.description: The ap_rwrite() function in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.53 and earlier may read unintended memory if an attacker can cause the server to reflect very large input using ap_rwrite() or ap_rputs(), such as with mod_luas r:puts() function.

vulnerabilities.name: Read beyond bounds in ap_strcmp_match()
vulnerabilities.description: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.53 and earlier may crash or disclose information due to a read beyond bounds in ap_strcmp_match() when provided with an extremely large input buffer. While no code distributed with the server can be coerced into such a call, third-party modules or lua scripts that use ap_strcmp_match() may hypothetically be affected.

vulnerabilities.name: Denial of service in mod_lua r:parsebody
vulnerabilities.description: In Apache HTTP Server 2.4.53 and earlier, a malicious request to a lua script that calls r:parsebody(0) may cause a denial of service due to no default limit on possible input size.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_sed denial of service
vulnerabilities.description: If Apache HTTP Server 2.4.53 is configured to do transformations with mod_sed in contexts where the input to mod_sed may be very large, mod_sed may make excessively large memory allocations and trigger an abort.

vulnerabilities.name: Information Disclosure in mod_lua with websockets
vulnerabilities.description: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.53 and earlier may return lengths to applications calling r:wsread() that point past the end of the storage allocated for the buffer.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy X-Forwarded-For dropped by hop-by-hop mechanism
vulnerabilities.description: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.53 and earlier may not send the X-Forwarded- headers to the origin server based on client side Connection header hop-by-hop mechanism. This may be used to bypass IP based authentication on the origin server/application.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_lua Use of uninitialized value of in r:parsebody
vulnerabilities.description: A carefully crafted request body can cause a read to a random memory area which could cause the process to crash.

vulnerabilities.name: HTTP request smuggling vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.52 and earlier
vulnerabilities.description: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.52 and earlier fails to close inbound connection when errors are encountered discarding the request body, exposing the server to HTTP Request Smuggling

vulnerabilities.name: core: Possible buffer overflow with very large or unlimited LimitXMLRequestBody
vulnerabilities.description: If LimitXMLRequestBody is set to allow request bodies larger than 350MB (defaults to 1M) on 32 bit systems an integer overflow happens which later causes out of bounds writes.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_sed: Read/write beyond bounds
vulnerabilities.description: Out-of-bounds Write vulnerability in mod_sed of Apache HTTP Server allows an attacker to overwrite heap memory with possibly attacker provided data.

vulnerabilities.name: Possible NULL dereference or SSRF in forward proxy configurations in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.51 and earlier
vulnerabilities.description: A crafted URI sent to httpd configured as a forward proxy (ProxyRequests on) can cause a crash (NULL pointer dereference) or, for configurations mixing forward and reverse proxy declarations, can allow for requests to be directed to a declared Unix Domain Socket endpoint (Server Side Request Forgery).

vulnerabilities.name: Possible buffer overflow when parsing multipart content in mod_lua of Apache HTTP Server 2.4.51 and earlier
vulnerabilities.description: A carefully crafted request body can cause a buffer overflow in the mod_lua multipart parser (r:parsebody() called from Lua scripts). The Apache httpd team is not aware of an exploit for the vulnerabilty though it might be possible to craft one.

vulnerabilities.name: Path Traversal and Remote Code Execution in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.49 and 2.4.50 (incomplete fix of CVE-2021-41773)
vulnerabilities.description: It was found that the fix for CVE-2021-41773 in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.50 was insufficient. An attacker could use a path traversal attack to map URLs to files outside the directories configured by Alias-like directives.

vulnerabilities.name: null pointer dereference in h2 fuzzing
vulnerabilities.description: While fuzzing the 2.4.49 httpd, a new null pointer dereference was detected during HTTP/2 request processing, allowing an external source to DoS the server. This requires a specially crafted request.

vulnerabilities.name: Path traversal and file disclosure vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.49
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in a change made to path normalization in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.49. An attacker could use a path traversal attack to map URLs to files outside the directories configured by Alias-like directives.

vulnerabilities.name: NULL pointer dereference in httpd core
vulnerabilities.description: Malformed requests may cause the server to dereference a NULL pointer.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_uwsgi out of bound read
vulnerabilities.description: A carefully crafted request uri-path can cause mod_proxy_uwsgi to read above the allocated memory and crash (DoS).

vulnerabilities.name: ap_escape_quotes buffer overflow
vulnerabilities.description: ap_escape_quotes() may write beyond the end of a buffer when given malicious input. No included modules pass untrusted data to these functions, but third-party / external modules may.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy SSRF
vulnerabilities.description: A crafted request uri-path can cause mod_proxy to forward the request to an origin server choosen by the remote user.

vulnerabilities.name: Request splitting via HTTP/2 method injection and mod_proxy
vulnerabilities.description: A crafted method sent through HTTP/2 will bypass validation and be forwarded by mod_proxy, which can lead to request splitting or cache poisoning.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_wstunnel tunneling of non Upgraded connections
vulnerabilities.description: Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.6 to 2.4.46 mod_proxy_wstunnel configured on an URL that is not necessarily Upgraded by the origin server was tunneling the whole connection regardless, thus allowing for subsequent requests on the same connection to pass through with no HTTP validation, authentication or authorization possibly configured.

vulnerabilities.name: Improper Handling of Insufficient Privileges
vulnerabilities.description: Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.0 to 2.4.46 Unprivileged local users can stop httpd on Windows

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_http NULL pointer dereference
vulnerabilities.description: Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.41 to 2.4.46 mod_proxy_http can be made to crash (NULL pointer dereference) with specially crafted requests using both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers, leading to a Denial of Service

vulnerabilities.name: mod_auth_digest possible stack overflow by one nul byte
vulnerabilities.description: Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.0 to 2.4.46 A specially crafted Digest nonce can cause a stack overflow in mod_auth_digest. There is no report of this overflow being exploitable, nor the Apache HTTP Server team could create one, though some particular compiler and/or compilation option might make it possible, with limited consequences anyway due to the size (a single byte) and the value (zero byte) of the overflow

vulnerabilities.name: mod_session NULL pointer dereference
vulnerabilities.description: Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.0 to 2.4.46 A specially crafted Cookie header handled by mod_session can cause a NULL pointer dereference and crash, leading to a possible Denial Of Service

vulnerabilities.name: mod_session response handling heap overflow
vulnerabilities.description: Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.0 to 2.4.46 A specially crafted SessionHeader sent by an origin server could cause a heap overflow

vulnerabilities.name: Unexpected URL matching with 'MergeSlashes OFF'
vulnerabilities.description: Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.39 to 2.4.46 Unexpected matching behavior with 'MergeSlashes OFF'

vulnerabilities.name: NULL pointer dereference on specially crafted HTTP/2 request
vulnerabilities.description: Apache HTTP Server protocol handler for the HTTP/2 protocol checks received request headers against the size limitations as configured for the server and used for the HTTP/1 protocol as well. On violation of these restrictions and HTTP response is sent to the client with a status code indicating why the request was rejected.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_uwsgi buffer overflow
vulnerabilities.description: In Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.32 to 2.4.43, mod_proxy_uwsgi has a information disclosure and possible RCE

vulnerabilities.name: IP address spoofing when proxying using mod_remoteip and mod_rewrite
vulnerabilities.description: For configurations using proxying with mod_remoteip and certain mod_rewrite rules, an attacker could spoof their IP address for logging and PHP scripts. Note this issue was fixed in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.24 but was retrospectively allocated a low severity CVE in 2020.

vulnerabilities.name: Push Diary Crash on Specifically Crafted HTTP/2 Header
vulnerabilities.description: In Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.20 to 2.4.43, when trace/debug was enabled for the HTTP/2 module and on certain traffic edge patterns, logging statements were made on the wrong connection, causing concurrent use of memory pools. Configuring the LogLevel of mod_http2 above "info" will mitigate this vulnerability for unpatched servers.

vulnerabilities.name: Push Diary Crash on Specifically Crafted HTTP/2 Header
vulnerabilities.description: In Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.20 to 2.4.43, a specially crafted value for the 'Cache-Digest' header in a HTTP/2 request would result in a crash when the server actually tries to HTTP/2 PUSH a resource afterwards. Configuring the HTTP/2 feature via "H2Push off" will mitigate this vulnerability for unpatched servers.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_rewrite CWE-601 open redirect
vulnerabilities.description: In Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.0 to 2.4.41 some mod_rewrite configurations vulnerable to open redirect.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_ftp use of uninitialized value
vulnerabilities.description: in Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.0 to 2.4.41, mod_proxy_ftp use of uninitialized value with malicious FTP backend.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_http2, memory corruption on early pushes
vulnerabilities.description: HTTP/2 very early pushes, for example configured with "H2PushResource", could lead to an overwrite of memory in the pushing request's pool, leading to crashes. The memory copied is that of the configured push link header values, not data supplied by the client.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_http2, read-after-free in h2 connection shutdown
vulnerabilities.description: Using fuzzed network input, the http/2 session handling could be made to read memory after being freed, during connection shutdown.

vulnerabilities.name: Limited cross-site scripting in mod_proxy error page
vulnerabilities.description: A limited cross-site scripting issue was reported affecting the mod_proxy error page. An attacker could cause the link on the error page to be malfomed and instead point to a page of their choice. This would only be exploitable where a server was set up with proxying enabled but was misconfigured in such a way that the Proxy Error page was displayed. We have taken this opportunity to also remove request data from many other in-built error messages. Note however this issue did not affect them...

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2019-10097 mod_remoteip: Stack buffer overflow and NULL pointer dereference
vulnerabilities.description: When mod_remoteip was configured to use a trusted intermediary proxy server using the "PROXY" protocol, a specially crafted PROXY header could trigger a stack buffer overflow or NULL pointer deference. This vulnerability could only be triggered by a trusted proxy and not by untrusted HTTP clients.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_rewrite potential open redirect
vulnerabilities.description: Redirects configured with mod_rewrite that were intended to be self-referential might be fooled by encoded newlines and redirect instead to an an unexpected URL within the request URL.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_http2, DoS attack by exhausting h2 workers.
vulnerabilities.description: A malicious client could perform a DoS attack by flooding a connection with requests and basically never reading responses on the TCP connection. Depending on h2 worker dimensioning, it was possible to block those with relatively few connections.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_http2, read-after-free on a string compare
vulnerabilities.description: Using fuzzed network input, the http/2 request handling could be made to access freed memory in string comparision when determining the method of a request and thus process the request incorrectly.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_http2, possible crash on late upgrade
vulnerabilities.description: When HTTP/2 was enabled for a http: host or H2Upgrade was enabled for h2 on a https: host, an Upgrade request from http/1.1 to http/2 that was not the first request on a connection could lead to a misconfiguration and crash. A server that never enabled the h2 protocol or that only enabled it for https: and did not configure the "H2Upgrade on" is unaffected by this.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Server privilege escalation from modules' scripts
vulnerabilities.description: In Apache HTTP Server 2.4 releases 2.4.17 to 2.4.38, with MPM event, worker or prefork, code executing in less-privileged child processes or threads (including scripts executed by an in-process scripting interpreter) could execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the parent process (usually root) by manipulating the scoreboard. Non-Unix systems are not affected.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_ssl access control bypass
vulnerabilities.description: In Apache HTTP Server 2.4 releases 2.4.37 and 2.4.38, a bug in mod_ssl when using per-location client certificate verification with TLSv1.3 allowed a client supporting Post-Handshake Authentication to bypass configured access control restrictions.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_auth_digest access control bypass
vulnerabilities.description: In Apache HTTP Server 2.4 release 2.4.38 and prior, a race condition in mod_auth_digest when running in a threaded server could allow a user with valid credentials to authenticate using another username, bypassing configured access control restrictions.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache httpd URL normalization inconsistincy
vulnerabilities.description: When the path component of a request URL contains multiple consecutive slashes ('/'), directives such as LocationMatch and RewriteRule must account for duplicates in regular expressions while other aspects of the servers processing will implicitly collapse them.

vulnerabilities.name: DoS for HTTP/2 connections via slow request bodies
vulnerabilities.description: By sending request bodies in a slow loris way to plain resources, the h2 stream for that request unnecessarily occupied a server thread cleaning up that incoming data. This affects only HTTP/2 connections. A possible mitigation is to not enable the h2 protocol.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_session_cookie does not respect expiry time
vulnerabilities.description: In Apache HTTP Server 2.4 release 2.4.37 and prior, mod_session checks the session expiry time before decoding the session. This causes session expiry time to be ignored for mod_session_cookie sessions since the expiry time is loaded when the session is decoded.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_ssl 2.4.37 remote DoS when used with OpenSSL 1.1.1
vulnerabilities.description: A bug exists in the way mod_ssl handled client renegotiations. A remote attacker could send a carefully crafted request that would cause mod_ssl to enter a loop leading to a denial of service. This bug can be only triggered with Apache HTTP Server version 2.4.37 when using OpenSSL version 1.1.1 or later, due to an interaction in changes to handling of renegotiation attempts.

vulnerabilities.name: DoS for HTTP/2 connections by continuous SETTINGS
vulnerabilities.description: By sending continous SETTINGS frames of maximum size an ongoing HTTP/2 connection could be kept busy and would never time out. This can be abused for a DoS on the server. This only affect a server that has enabled the h2 protocol.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_userdir CRLF injection
vulnerabilities.description: Possible CRLF injection allowing HTTP response splitting attacks for sites which use mod_userdir. This issue was mitigated by changes made in 2.4.25 and 2.2.32 which prohibit CR or LF injection into the "Location" or other outbound header key or value.

vulnerabilities.name: DoS for HTTP/2 connections by crafted requests
vulnerabilities.description: By specially crafting HTTP/2 requests, workers would be allocated 60 seconds longer than necessary, leading to worker exhaustion and a denial of service. This issue only affects servers that have configured and enabled HTTP/2 support, which is not the default

vulnerabilities.name: mod_md, DoS via Coredumps on specially crafted requests
vulnerabilities.description: By specially crafting HTTP requests, the mod_md challenge handler would dereference a NULL pointer and cause the child process to segfault. This could be used to DoS the server.

vulnerabilities.name: Out of bound write in mod_authnz_ldap when using too small Accept-Language values
vulnerabilities.description: mod_authnz_ldap, if configured with AuthLDAPCharsetConfig, uses the Accept-Language header value to lookup the right charset encoding when verifying the user's credentials. If the header value is not present in the charset conversion table, a fallback mechanism is used to truncate it to a two characters value to allow a quick retry (for example, 'en-US' is truncated to 'en'). A header value of less than two characters forces an out of bound write of one NUL byte to a memory location that is not...

vulnerabilities.name: <FilesMatch> bypass with a trailing newline in the file name
vulnerabilities.description: The expression specified in <FilesMatch> could match '$' to a newline character in a malicious filename, rather than matching only the end of the filename. This could be exploited in environments where uploads of some files are are externally blocked, but only by matching the trailing portion of the filename.

vulnerabilities.name: Tampering of mod_session data for CGI applications
vulnerabilities.description: When mod_session is configured to forward its session data to CGI applications (SessionEnv on, not the default), a remote user may influence their content by using a "Session" header. This comes from the "HTTP_SESSION" variable name used by mod_session to forward its data to CGIs, since the prefix "HTTP_" is also used by the Apache HTTP Server to pass HTTP header fields, per CGI specifications. The severity is set to Moderate because "SessionEnv on" is not a default nor common configuration, it...

vulnerabilities.name: Possible out of bound access after failure in reading the HTTP request
vulnerabilities.description: A specially crafted request could have crashed the Apache HTTP Server prior to version 2.4.33, due to an out of bound access after a size limit is reached by reading the HTTP header. This vulnerability is considered very hard if not impossible to trigger in non-debug mode (both log and build level), so it is classified as low risk for common server usage.

vulnerabilities.name: Possible write of after free on HTTP/2 stream shutdown
vulnerabilities.description: When an HTTP/2 stream was destroyed after being handled, the Apache HTTP Server prior to version 2.4.33 could have written a NULL pointer potentially to an already freed memory. The memory pools maintained by the server make this vulnerabilty hard to trigger in usual configurations, the reporter and the team could not reproduce it outside debug builds, so it is classified as low risk.

vulnerabilities.name: Possible out of bound read in mod_cache_socache
vulnerabilities.description: A specially crafted HTTP request header could have crashed the Apache HTTP Server prior to version 2.4.33 due to an out of bound read while preparing data to be cached in shared memory. It could be used as a Denial of Service attack against users of mod_cache_socache.

vulnerabilities.name: Weak Digest auth nonce generation in mod_auth_digest
vulnerabilities.description: When generating an HTTP Digest authentication challenge, the nonce sent to prevent reply attacks was not correctly generated using a pseudo-random seed. In a cluster of servers using a common Digest authentication configuration, HTTP requests could be replayed across servers by an attacker without detection.

vulnerabilities.name: Use-after-free when using <Limit > with an unrecognized method in .htaccess ("OptionsBleed")
vulnerabilities.description: When an unrecognized HTTP Method is given in an <Limit {method}> directive in an .htaccess file, and that .htaccess file is processed by the corresponding request, the global methods table is corrupted in the current worker process, resulting in erratic behaviour. This behavior may be avoided by listing all unusual HTTP Methods in a global httpd.conf RegisterHttpMethod directive in httpd release 2.4.25 and later. To permit other .htaccess directives while denying the <Limit > directive, see the...

vulnerabilities.name: Uninitialized memory reflection in mod_auth_digest
vulnerabilities.description: The value placeholder in [Proxy-]Authorization headers of type 'Digest' was not initialized or reset before or between successive key=value assignments. by mod_auth_digest. Providing an initial key with no '=' assignment could reflect the stale value of uninitialized pool memory used by the prior request, leading to leakage of potentially confidential information, and a segfault.

vulnerabilities.name: Read after free in mod_http2
vulnerabilities.description: When under stress, closing many connections, the HTTP/2 handling code would sometimes access memory after it has been freed, resulting in potentially erratic behaviour.

vulnerabilities.name: ap_get_basic_auth_pw() Authentication Bypass
vulnerabilities.description: Use of the ap_get_basic_auth_pw() by third-party modules outside of the authentication phase may lead to authentication requirements being bypassed. Third-party module writers SHOULD use ap_get_basic_auth_components(), available in 2.2.34 and 2.4.26, instead of ap_get_basic_auth_pw(). Modules which call the legacy ap_get_basic_auth_pw() during the authentication phase MUST either immediately authenticate the user after the call, or else stop the request immediately with an error response, to...

vulnerabilities.name: mod_ssl Null Pointer Dereference
vulnerabilities.description: mod_ssl may dereference a NULL pointer when third-party modules call ap_hook_process_connection() during an HTTP request to an HTTPS port.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_http2 Null Pointer Dereference
vulnerabilities.description: A maliciously constructed HTTP/2 request could cause mod_http2 to dereference a NULL pointer and crash the server process.

vulnerabilities.name: ap_find_token() Buffer Overread
vulnerabilities.description: The HTTP strict parsing changes added in 2.2.32 and 2.4.24 introduced a bug in token list parsing, which allows ap_find_token() to search past the end of its input string. By maliciously crafting a sequence of request headers, an attacker may be able to cause a segmentation fault, or to force ap_find_token() to return an incorrect value.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_mime Buffer Overread
vulnerabilities.description: mod_mime can read one byte past the end of a buffer when sending a malicious Content-Type response header.

vulnerabilities.name: Padding Oracle in Apache mod_session_crypto
vulnerabilities.description: Prior to Apache HTTP release 2.4.25, mod_sessioncrypto was encrypting its data/cookie using the configured ciphers with possibly either CBC or ECB modes of operation (AES256-CBC by default), hence no selectable or builtin authenticated encryption. This made it vulnerable to padding oracle attacks, particularly with CBC. An authentication tag (SipHash MAC) is now added to prevent such attacks.

vulnerabilities.name: DoS vulnerability in mod_auth_digest
vulnerabilities.description: Malicious input to mod_auth_digest will cause the server to crash, and each instance continues to crash even for subsequently valid requests.

vulnerabilities.name: Apache HTTP Request Parsing Whitespace Defects
vulnerabilities.description: Apache HTTP Server, prior to release 2.4.25 (and 2.2.32), accepted a broad pattern of unusual whitespace patterns from the user-agent, including bare CR, FF, VTAB in parsing the request line and request header lines, as well as HTAB in parsing the request line. Any bare CR present in request lines was treated as whitespace and remained in the request field member "the_request", while a bare CR in the request header field name would be honored as whitespace, and a bare CR in the request header...

vulnerabilities.name: HTTP/2 CONTINUATION denial of service
vulnerabilities.description: The HTTP/2 protocol implementation (mod_http2) had an incomplete handling of the LimitRequestFields directive. This allowed an attacker to inject unlimited request headers into the server, leading to eventual memory exhaustion.

vulnerabilities.name: TLS/SSL X.509 client certificate auth bypass with HTTP/2
vulnerabilities.description: For configurations enabling support for HTTP/2, SSL client certificate validation was not enforced if configured, allowing clients unauthorized access to protected resources over HTTP/2. This issue affected releases 2.4.18 and 2.4.20 only.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_http2: denial of service by thread starvation
vulnerabilities.description: By manipulating the flow control windows on streams, a client was able to block server threads for long times, causing starvation of worker threads. Connections could still be opened, but no streams where processed for these. This issue affected HTTP/2 support in 2.4.17 and 2.4.18.

vulnerabilities.name: HTTP request smuggling attack against chunked request parser
vulnerabilities.description: An HTTP request smuggling attack was possible due to a bug in parsing of chunked requests. A malicious client could force the server to misinterpret the request length, allowing cache poisoning or credential hijacking if an intermediary proxy is in use.

vulnerabilities.name: ap_some_auth_required API unusable
vulnerabilities.description: A design error in the "ap_some_auth_required" function renders the API unusuable in httpd 2.4.x. In particular the API is documented to answering if the request required authentication but only answers if there are Require lines in the applicable configuration. Since 2.4.x Require lines are used for authorization as well and can appear in configurations even when no authentication is required and the request is entirely unrestricted. This could lead to modules using this API to allow access when...

vulnerabilities.name: Crash in ErrorDocument 400 handling
vulnerabilities.description: A crash in ErrorDocument handling was found. If ErrorDocument 400 was configured pointing to a local URL-path with the INCLUDES filter active, a NULL dereference would occur when handling the error, causing the child process to crash. This issue affected the 2.4.12 release only.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_lua: Crash in websockets PING handling
vulnerabilities.description: A stack recursion crash in the mod_lua module was found. A Lua script executing the r:wsupgrade() function could crash the process if a malicious client sent a carefully crafted PING request. This issue affected releases 2.4.7 through 2.4.12 inclusive.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_fcgi out-of-bounds memory read
vulnerabilities.description: An out-of-bounds memory read was found in mod_proxy_fcgi. A malicious FastCGI server could send a carefully crafted response which could lead to a crash when reading past the end of a heap memory or stack buffer. This issue affects version 2.4.10 only.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_lua multiple "Require" directive handling is broken
vulnerabilities.description: Fix handling of the Require line in mod_lua when a LuaAuthzProvider is used in multiple Require directives with different arguments. This could lead to different authentication rules than expected.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_cache crash with empty Content-Type header
vulnerabilities.description: A NULL pointer deference was found in mod_cache. A malicious HTTP server could cause a crash in a caching forward proxy configuration. This crash would only be a denial of service if using a threaded MPM.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy denial of service
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in mod_proxy in httpd versions 2.4.6 to 2.4.9. A remote attacker could send a carefully crafted request to a server configured as a reverse proxy, and cause the child process to crash. This could lead to a denial of service against a threaded MPM.

vulnerabilities.name: WinNT MPM denial of service
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the WinNT MPM in httpd versions 2.4.1 to 2.4.9, when using the default AcceptFilter for that platform. A remote attacker could send carefully crafted requests that would leak memory and eventually lead to a denial of service against the server.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_cache crash
vulnerabilities.description: A NULL pointer dereference was found in mod_cache. A malicious HTTP server could cause a crash in a caching forward proxy configuration. (Note that this vulnerability was fixed in the 2.4.7 release, but the security impact was not disclosed at the time of the release.)

vulnerabilities.name: mod_deflate denial of service
vulnerabilities.description: A resource consumption flaw was found in mod_deflate. If request body decompression was configured (using the "DEFLATE" input filter), a remote attacker could cause the server to consume significant memory and/or CPU resources. The use of request body decompression is not a common configuration.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_status buffer overflow
vulnerabilities.description: A race condition was found in mod_status. An attacker able to access a public server status page on a server using a threaded MPM could send a carefully crafted request which could lead to a heap buffer overflow. Note that it is not a default or recommended configuration to have a public accessible server status page.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_cgid denial of service
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in mod_cgid. If a server using mod_cgid hosted CGI scripts which did not consume standard input, a remote attacker could cause child processes to hang indefinitely, leading to denial of service.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_dav crash
vulnerabilities.description: XML parsing code in mod_dav incorrectly calculates the end of the string when removing leading spaces and places a NUL character outside the buffer, causing random crashes. This XML parsing code is only used with DAV provider modules that support DeltaV, of which the only publicly released provider is mod_dav_svn.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_log_config crash
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in mod_log_config. A remote attacker could send a specific truncated cookie causing a crash. This crash would only be a denial of service if using a threaded MPM.

vulnerabilities.name: HTTP Trailers processing bypass
vulnerabilities.description: HTTP trailers could be used to replace HTTP headers late during request processing, potentially undoing or otherwise confusing modules that examined or modified request headers earlier. This fix adds the "MergeTrailers" directive to restore legacy behavior.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_session_dbd session fixation flaw
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw in mod_session_dbd caused it to proceed with save operations for a session without considering the dirty flag and the requirement for a new session ID.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_dav crash
vulnerabilities.description: Sending a MERGE request against a URI handled by mod_dav_svn with the source href (sent as part of the request body as XML) pointing to a URI that is not configured for DAV will trigger a segfault.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_rewrite log escape filtering
vulnerabilities.description: mod_rewrite does not filter terminal escape sequences from logs, which could make it easier for attackers to insert those sequences into terminal emulators containing vulnerabilities related to escape sequences.

vulnerabilities.name: XSS due to unescaped hostnames
vulnerabilities.description: Various XSS flaws due to unescaped hostnames and URIs HTML output in mod_info, mod_status, mod_imagemap, mod_ldap, and mod_proxy_ftp.

vulnerabilities.name: XSS in mod_proxy_balancer
vulnerabilities.description: A XSS flaw affected the mod_proxy_balancer manager interface.

vulnerabilities.name: Response mixup when using mod_proxy_ajp or mod_proxy_http
vulnerabilities.description: The modules mod_proxy_ajp and mod_proxy_http did not always close the connection to the back end server when necessary as part of error handling. This could lead to an information disclosure due to a response mixup between users.

vulnerabilities.name: XSS in mod_negotiation when untrusted uploads are supported
vulnerabilities.description: Possible XSS for sites which use mod_negotiation and allow untrusted uploads to locations which have MultiViews enabled. Note: This issue is also known as CVE-2008-0455.

vulnerabilities.name: insecure LD_LIBRARY_PATH handling
vulnerabilities.description: Insecure handling of LD_LIBRARY_PATH was found that could lead to the current working directory to be searched for DSOs. This could allow a local user to execute code as root if an administrator runs apachectl from an untrusted directory.

vulnerabilities.name: error responses can expose cookies
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the default error response for status code 400. This flaw could be used by an attacker to expose "httpOnly" cookies when no custom ErrorDocument is specified.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy reverse proxy exposure
vulnerabilities.description: An additional exposure was found when using mod_proxy in reverse proxy mode. In certain configurations using RewriteRule with proxy flag or ProxyPassMatch, a remote attacker could cause the reverse proxy to connect to an arbitrary server, possibly disclosing sensitive information from internal web servers not directly accessible to attacker.

vulnerabilities.name: scoreboard parent DoS
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the handling of the scoreboard. An unprivileged child process could cause the parent process to crash at shutdown rather than terminate cleanly.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_ajp remote DoS
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found when mod_proxy_ajp connects to a backend server that takes too long to respond. Given a specific configuration, a remote attacker could send certain requests, putting a backend server into an error state until the retry timeout expired. This could lead to a temporary denial of service.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_log_config crash
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in mod_log_config. If the '%{cookiename}C' log format string is in use, a remote attacker could send a specific cookie causing a crash. This crash would only be a denial of service if using a threaded MPM.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_setenvif .htaccess privilege escalation
vulnerabilities.description: An integer overflow flaw was found which, when the mod_setenvif module is enabled, could allow local users to gain privileges via a .htaccess file.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy reverse proxy exposure
vulnerabilities.description: An exposure was found when using mod_proxy in reverse proxy mode. In certain configurations using RewriteRule with proxy flag or ProxyPassMatch, a remote attacker could cause the reverse proxy to connect to an arbitrary server, possibly disclosing sensitive information from internal web servers not directly accessible to attacker. No update of 1.3 will be released. Patches will be published to https://archive.apache.org/dist/httpd/patches/apply_to_1.3.42/

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_ajp remote DoS
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found when mod_proxy_ajp is used together with mod_proxy_balancer. Given a specific configuration, a remote attacker could send certain malformed HTTP requests, putting a backend server into an error state until the retry timeout expired. This could lead to a temporary denial of service.

vulnerabilities.name: Range header remote DoS
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the way the Apache HTTP Server handled Range HTTP headers. A remote attacker could use this flaw to cause httpd to use an excessive amount of memory and CPU time via HTTP requests with a specially-crafted Range header. This could be used in a denial of service attack. Advisory: CVE-2011-3192.txt

vulnerabilities.name: apr_fnmatch flaw leads to mod_autoindex remote DoS
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the apr_fnmatch() function of the bundled APR library. Where mod_autoindex is enabled, and a directory indexed by mod_autoindex contained files with sufficiently long names, a remote attacker could send a carefully crafted request which would cause excessive CPU usage. This could be used in a denial of service attack. Workaround: Setting the 'IgnoreClient' option to the 'IndexOptions' directive disables processing of the client-supplied request query arguments, preventing...

vulnerabilities.name: apr_bridage_split_line DoS
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the apr_brigade_split_line() function of the bundled APR-util library, used to process non-SSL requests. A remote attacker could send requests, carefully crafting the timing of individual bytes, which would slowly consume memory, potentially leading to a denial of service.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_cache and mod_dav DoS
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the handling of requests by mod_cache (2.2) and mod_dav (2.0 and 2.2). A malicious remote attacker could send a carefully crafted request and cause a httpd child process to crash. This crash would only be a denial of service if using the worker MPM. This issue is further mitigated as mod_dav is only affected by requests that are most likely to be authenticated, and mod_cache is only affected if the uncommon "CacheIgnoreURLSessionIdentifiers" directive, introduced in version...

vulnerabilities.name: Timeout detection flaw (mod_proxy_http)
vulnerabilities.description: An information disclosure flaw was found in mod_proxy_http in version 2.2.9 only, on Unix platforms. Under certain timeout conditions, the server could return a response intended for another user. Only those configurations which trigger the use of proxy worker pools are affected. There was no vulnerability on earlier versions, as proxy pools were not yet introduced. The simplest workaround is to globally configure: SetEnv proxy-nokeepalive 1

vulnerabilities.name: Timeout detection flaw (mod_proxy_http)
vulnerabilities.description: An information disclosure flaw was found in mod_proxy_http in versions 2.2.9 through 2.2.15, 2.3.4-alpha and 2.3.5-alpha. Under certain timeout conditions, the server could return a response intended for another user. Only Windows, Netware and OS2 operating systems are affected. Only those configurations which trigger the use of proxy worker pools are affected. There was no vulnerability on earlier versions, as proxy pools were not yet introduced. The simplest workaround is to globally...

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_ajp DoS
vulnerabilities.description: mod_proxy_ajp would return the wrong status code if it encountered an error, causing a backend server to be put into an error state until the retry timeout expired. A remote attacker could send malicious requests to trigger this issue, resulting in denial of service.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_isapi module unload flaw
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found with within mod_isapi which would attempt to unload the ISAPI dll when it encountered various error states. This could leave the callbacks in an undefined state and result in a segfault. On Windows platforms using mod_isapi, a remote attacker could send a malicious request to trigger this issue, and as win32 MPM runs only one process, this would result in a denial of service, and potentially allow arbitrary code execution.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy overflow on 64-bit systems
vulnerabilities.description: An incorrect conversion between numeric types flaw was found in the mod_proxy module which affects some 64-bit architecture systems. A malicious HTTP server to which requests are being proxied could use this flaw to trigger a heap buffer overflow in an httpd child process via a carefully crafted response.

vulnerabilities.name: Subrequest handling of request headers (mod_headers)
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw in the core subrequest process code was fixed, to always provide a shallow copy of the headers_in array to the subrequest, instead of a pointer to the parent request's array as it had for requests without request bodies. This meant all modules such as mod_headers which may manipulate the input headers for a subrequest would poison the parent request in two ways, one by modifying the parent request, which might not be intended, and second by leaving pointers to modified header fields in...

vulnerabilities.name: expat DoS
vulnerabilities.description: A buffer over-read flaw was found in the bundled expat library. An attacker who is able to get Apache to parse an untrused XML document (for example through mod_dav) may be able to cause a crash. This crash would only be a denial of service if using the worker MPM.

vulnerabilities.name: Solaris pollset DoS
vulnerabilities.description: Faulty error handling was found affecting Solaris pollset support (Event Port backend) caused by a bug in APR. A remote attacker could trigger this issue on Solaris servers which used prefork or event MPMs, resulting in a denial of service.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_ftp FTP command injection
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the mod_proxy_ftp module. In a reverse proxy configuration, a remote attacker could use this flaw to bypass intended access restrictions by creating a carefully-crafted HTTP Authorization header, allowing the attacker to send arbitrary commands to the FTP server.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_ftp DoS
vulnerabilities.description: A NULL pointer dereference flaw was found in the mod_proxy_ftp module. A malicious FTP server to which requests are being proxied could use this flaw to crash an httpd child process via a malformed reply to the EPSV or PASV commands, resulting in a limited denial of service.

vulnerabilities.name: APR apr_palloc heap overflow
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw in apr_palloc() in the bundled copy of APR could cause heap overflows in programs that try to apr_palloc() a user controlled size. The Apache HTTP Server itself does not pass unsanitized user-provided sizes to this function, so it could only be triggered through some other application which uses apr_palloc() in a vulnerable way.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy reverse proxy DoS
vulnerabilities.description: A denial of service flaw was found in the mod_proxy module when it was used as a reverse proxy. A remote attacker could use this flaw to force a proxy process to consume large amounts of CPU time.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_deflate DoS
vulnerabilities.description: A denial of service flaw was found in the mod_deflate module. This module continued to compress large files until compression was complete, even if the network connection that requested the content was closed before compression completed. This would cause mod_deflate to consume large amounts of CPU if mod_deflate was enabled for a large file.

vulnerabilities.name: APR-util heap underwrite
vulnerabilities.description: A heap-based underwrite flaw was found in the way the bundled copy of the APR-util library created compiled forms of particular search patterns. An attacker could formulate a specially-crafted search keyword, that would overwrite arbitrary heap memory locations when processed by the pattern preparation engine.

vulnerabilities.name: APR-util XML DoS
vulnerabilities.description: A denial of service flaw was found in the bundled copy of the APR-util library Extensible Markup Language (XML) parser. A remote attacker could create a specially-crafted XML document that would cause excessive memory consumption when processed by the XML decoding engine.

vulnerabilities.name: APR-util off-by-one overflow
vulnerabilities.description: An off-by-one overflow flaw was found in the way the bundled copy of the APR-util library processed a variable list of arguments. An attacker could provide a specially-crafted string as input for the formatted output conversion routine, which could, on big-endian platforms, potentially lead to the disclosure of sensitive information or a denial of service.

vulnerabilities.name: AllowOverride Options handling bypass
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the handling of the "Options" and "AllowOverride" directives. In configurations using the "AllowOverride" directive with certain "Options=" arguments, local users were not restricted from executing commands from a Server-Side-Include script as intended.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_ajp information disclosure
vulnerabilities.description: An information disclosure flaw was found in mod_proxy_ajp in version 2.2.11 only. In certain situations, if a user sent a carefully crafted HTTP request, the server could return a response intended for another user.

vulnerabilities.name: expat DoS
vulnerabilities.description: A buffer over-read flaw was found in the bundled expat library. An attacker who is able to get Apache to parse an untrused XML document (for example through mod_dav) may be able to cause a crash. This crash would only be a denial of service if using the worker MPM.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_ftp globbing XSS
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the handling of wildcards in the path of a FTP URL with mod_proxy_ftp. If mod_proxy_ftp is enabled to support FTP-over-HTTP, requests containing globbing characters could lead to cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_http DoS
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the handling of excessive interim responses from an origin server when using mod_proxy_http. A remote attacker could cause a denial of service or high memory usage.

vulnerabilities.name: CRLF injection in mod_negotiation when untrusted uploads are supported
vulnerabilities.description: Possible CRLF injection allowing HTTP response splitting attacks for sites which use mod_negotiation and allow untrusted uploads to locations which have MultiViews enabled.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_balancer CSRF
vulnerabilities.description: The mod_proxy_balancer provided an administrative interface that could be vulnerable to cross-site request forgery (CSRF) attacks.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_ftp UTF-7 XSS
vulnerabilities.description: A workaround was added in the mod_proxy_ftp module. On sites where mod_proxy_ftp is enabled and a forward proxy is configured, a cross-site scripting attack is possible against Web browsers which do not correctly derive the response character set following the rules in RFC 2616.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_status XSS
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the mod_status module. On sites where mod_status is enabled and the status pages were publicly accessible, a cross-site scripting attack is possible. Note that the server-status page is not enabled by default and it is best practice to not make this publicly available.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_balancer XSS
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the mod_proxy_balancer module. On sites where mod_proxy_balancer is enabled, a cross-site scripting attack against an authorized user is possible.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy_balancer DoS
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the mod_proxy_balancer module. On sites where mod_proxy_balancer is enabled, an authorized user could send a carefully crafted request that would cause the Apache child process handling that request to crash. This could lead to a denial of service if using a threaded Multi-Processing Module.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_imagemap XSS
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the mod_imagemap module. On sites where mod_imagemap is enabled and an imagemap file is publicly available, a cross-site scripting attack is possible.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_status cross-site scripting
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the mod_status module. On sites where the server-status page is publicly accessible and ExtendedStatus is enabled this could lead to a cross-site scripting attack. Note that the server-status page is not enabled by default and it is best practice to not make this publicly available.

vulnerabilities.name: Signals to arbitrary processes
vulnerabilities.description: The Apache HTTP server did not verify that a process was an Apache child process before sending it signals. A local attacker with the ability to run scripts on the HTTP server could manipulate the scoreboard and cause arbitrary processes to be terminated which could lead to a denial of service.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_cache proxy DoS
vulnerabilities.description: A bug was found in the mod_cache module. On sites where caching is enabled, a remote attacker could send a carefully crafted request that would cause the Apache child process handling that request to crash. This could lead to a denial of service if using a threaded Multi-Processing Module.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_cache information leak
vulnerabilities.description: The recall_headers function in mod_mem_cache in Apache 2.2.4 did not properly copy all levels of header data, which can cause Apache to return HTTP headers containing previously used data, which could be used by remote attackers to obtain potentially sensitive information.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_proxy crash
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the Apache HTTP Server mod_proxy module. On sites where a reverse proxy is configured, a remote attacker could send a carefully crafted request that would cause the Apache child process handling that request to crash. On sites where a forward proxy is configured, an attacker could cause a similar crash if a user could be persuaded to visit a malicious site using the proxy. This could lead to a denial of service if using a threaded Multi-Processing Module.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_rewrite off-by-one error
vulnerabilities.description: An off-by-one flaw exists in the Rewrite module, mod_rewrite. Depending on the manner in which Apache httpd was compiled, this software defect may result in a vulnerability which, in combination with certain types of Rewrite rules in the web server configuration files, could be triggered remotely. For vulnerable builds, the nature of the vulnerability can be denial of service (crashing of web server processes) or potentially allow arbitrary code execution.

vulnerabilities.name: Expect header Cross-Site Scripting
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw in the handling of invalid Expect headers. If an attacker can influence the Expect header that a victim sends to a target site they could perform a cross-site scripting attack. It is known that some versions of Flash can set an arbitrary Expect header which can trigger this flaw. Not marked as a security issue for 2.0 or 2.2 as the cross-site scripting is only returned to the victim after the server times out a connection.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_imap Referer Cross-Site Scripting
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw in mod_imap when using the Referer directive with image maps. In certain site configurations a remote attacker could perform a cross-site scripting attack if a victim can be forced to visit a malicious URL using certain web browsers.

vulnerabilities.name: mod_ssl access control DoS
